item.title: Bayern draw up four-man shortlist to find backup and competition for Díaz
item.description: Bayern draw up four-man shortlist to find backup and competition for Díaz Currently lacking a natural alternative to Luis Díaz on the left wing, Bayern Munich are reportedly considering a move for a young winger who could provide backup and competition for the Colombian international ahead of next summer. According to Bild's Bayern Insider podcast, the German champions have four young wingers on their radar: Oskar Pietuszewski (FC Porto) , Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool) , Antonio Nusa (RB Leipzig) and Wael Mohya (Borussia Mönchengladbach) . Pietuszewski, an 18-year-old Polish winger, is reportedly at the top of Bayern's shortlist after impressing the club's scouting department in recent months. The youngster, who only joined Porto from Polish side Jagiellonia Białystok in January, is understood to have a €60 million release clause in his contract. As for Ngumoha, Bayern were already showing interest in the Liverpool youngster last summer and were reportedly prepared to offer €72 million for the 18-year-old. However, the Reds were unwilling to let him leave at the time. With Ngumoha under contract until 2028, the situation could potentially change next summer. Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl is said to be a particularly big admirer of Antonio Nusa. However, a move for the 21-year-old RB Leipzig star would also be expensive, potentially costing even more than either of the two aforementioned youngsters. Finally, 17-year-old Wael Mohya, who recently received his first senior Germany call-up, is also reportedly on Bayern's radar. The Bavarians have apparently been in contact with the youngster's representatives for some time. With Díaz currently sidelined, Alphonso Davies has recently filled in on the left wing for Bayern, while Nathaniel Brown could be deployed there against Mainz this weekend if the Canada international is deemed in need of a rest.

item.description: Jude and Jobe Bellingham could be the first brothers to play together for England since Gary and Phil Neville 19 years ago [Getty Images] It may be a surprise to some but Jobe Bellingham's call-up to the England senior side has been a long time coming. Jobe's career path has been very similar to that of his older brother Jude - England's star player at the World Cup and one of Real Madrid's best players. Both were stars of the Birmingham City academy before big-money moves to the German Bundesliga and England call-ups. Jobe's debut for Birmingham came at the age of 16 years and 107 days - 69 days older than Jude when he made his first appearance for the Blues' senior side. The central midfielder then moved to Sunderland and helped them win promotion to the Premier League before joining German side Borussia Dortmund at the age of 19 in a deal worth up to £31m. Jude also moved to Dortmund when he was 17, before developing into one of the world's best players and joining Real Madrid. Having one of the best midfielders in the world as your older brother comes with challenges and Jobe has consistently been compared to his sibling. But the former Sunderland midfielder is his own player, wearing 'Jobe' on the back of his shirt instead of his family name. He said it was suggested to him by a former coach because "it shows that I'm going my own way". Jobe is a different type of player to Jude, sitting deeper in the midfield, but is as physically imposing while still being good on the ball. He is the current captain of the England Under-21 side, and England manager Thomas Tuchel said Young Lions head coach Lee Carsley had been pushing for some time for the younger Bellingham to get senior recognition. "He's the standout player," said Tuchel. "He's the captain, so the door should always be open for the pathway, always be open for special performances over a long period of time. "That's what Jobe has done on top of it. He found his way, he found his rhythm with Dortmund. He's had an excellent start to his season, is a regular starter and influential." item.title: Confirmed: Cole Palmer left out of England squad again
item.description: Confirmed: Cole Palmer left out of England squad again England Squad Verdict: Cole Palmer Misses Out as Thomas Tuchel Turns to Youth Thomas Tuchel has made his call, and Cole Palmer is out. After medical checks and fresh discussion over his fitness, the Chelsea attacker has been omitted from England’s latest squad for the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. It is a big decision, and a pointed one. Palmer had already been warned by Tuchel after withdrawing from the previous camp. The England manager said he misses “too many opportunities” to play for his country because of injury. Chelsea maintain they told the Football Association that Palmer was fit and available if selected. In the end, that made no difference. Tuchel Sends Clear Palmer Message This feels less like a fitness issue and more like a managerial line in the sand. International football gives coaches limited time and limited patience. If Tuchel believes availability is becoming a pattern, he will move on quickly. Palmer is talented, no question, but talent does not guarantee selection. Photo IMAGO There was no room either for Arsenal winger Noni Madueke, while Phil Foden again misses out. Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo is absent too, after injury disrupted his last involvement and after a summer in which he was the only outfield player in Tuchel’s World Cup squad not to play a single minute. England Squad Opens Door for Jobe Bellingham The headlines elsewhere belong to the newcomers. Jobe Bellingham is in, Josh King is in, and both are uncapped. So too is Jason Steele, who keeps his place in the squad despite Dean Henderson returning at club level. Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha also gets the nod, alongside Inter Milan full-back Djed Spence and Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold. It is a squad with a definite youth slant, though not without experience. Harry Kane is there, of course, and on the verge of history. If he plays against Croatia at Wembley next Thursday, he will become England’s most-capped men’s player outright with appearance number 126. He had already drawn level with Peter Shilton on 125 during the 3-0 win over the Czech Republic. Harry Kane Record Chase Adds Weight Tuchel also welcomes back Declan Rice and Ben White after injury. Marcus Rashford and Bukayo Saka are unavailable, both ruled out through injury, while Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall remains overlooked despite external backing for his inclusion. That is the bottom line. Palmer misses out, Kane closes in on a landmark, and Tuchel has picked a squad that rewards availability, trusts form and leaves no room for sentiment.

item.title: What NFL chiefs have changed for Sunday’s game in Spain after ‘learning’ from last year’s mistake
item.description: Photo By Irina R. Hipolito/Europa Press via Getty Images The NFL’s international series picks up again this weekend as the Atlanta Falcons host the Cincinnati Bengals over in Spain, Madrid. Playing on foreign soil has divided NFL fans in the United States, with the Atlanta Falcons losing one of their home games as a result. A total of nine international games are being played this year, with two more following Sunday’s game in the Spanish capital. Last year saw the first-ever international game played in Spain at the home of Real Madrid, the Santiago Bernabeu. This time around, the NFL have admitted they have made some improvements ahead of Sunday’s game after learning from some of their errors made last year. NFL chiefs increase locker room sizes for Madrid game Over recent hours, some NFL fans have shared their concerns over the small locker rooms being used at the soccer stadium. Despite this, it has been claimed by the NFL that they have actually taken measures to increase the size of the locker rooms in Madrid. “A stadium that’s hosted everything from concerts to World Cup finals: for NFL games, maybe the most change happens in the locker rooms,” said reporter Victor Prieto. “Obviously, switching a locker room from soccer to football isn’t the easiest thing. There are a lot more players on a football team, but they say they learned a lot from last year’s game in Madrid, and they expanded the locker room this year, getting everything ready for the Falcons.” The reality is the Bernabeu was not built with hosting NFL games in mind. Unlike the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, the home of Real Madrid does not have NFL locker rooms built to accommodate the yearly game hosted in the stadium. One thing that has impressed those travelling over to Madrid for the game, though, is Madrid’s incredible turf system that produces fresh turf from four storeys below the surface. “Right here, fieldside at the Bernabeu, you see they’re getting the finishing touches out on the field. In this iconic stadium, perhaps what’s most unique about it is actually underground: Real Madrid uses real grass for its stadium, but stores it in a facility four storeys under the stadium called the hypogeum. The NFL brought a crew of 14 to work alongside Real Madrid’s field staff to get the pitch in football shape,” Prieto added. item.title: CBP Seizes Shipment Of 75 Counterfeit Super Bowl Rings From China
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) said officers in Texas recently seized a shipment of 75 counterfeit Kansas City Chiefs Super Bowl championship rings. CBP officers assigned to Houston’s George Bush Intercontinental Airport on Oct. 30 encountered an express consignment parcel from Guangzhou, China, manifested as “Hair Pins Metal.” Instead, the package contained what appeared to be the Chiefs Super Bowl rings. Officers noted the “poor craftsmanship” of the rings, however, and detained the rings to verify authenticity with the National Football League, which is the trademark holder. The NFL confirmed the rings were fake. U.S. Customs and Border Protection Had the rings been genuine, they would have been valued at $750,000 “at least,” CBP said. The shipment was seized. “Legitimate American businesses are often harmed by these global criminal organizations,” said CBP Acting Director of Field Operations Leslie Fleming-Luczkowski . “The sale of fake goods often funds money laundering, drug trafficking, and other illegal activities. CBP is on the front lines to ensure we protect the American people from defrauders while protecting businesses who play by the rules.” CBP said its officers in Houston have made “significant seizures” of counterfeit items in recent months, including watches, baby toys, and FIFA World Cup memorabilia and apparel. The Pacers are getting a sobering reminder of how fragile NBA success can be
item.description: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is tempting to hand-waive everything that has happened to the Indiana Pacers in the last year and a half as simply the work of some vengeful spirit, unfairly punishing an innocent fanbase who never did anything to deserve this kind of sustained injury catastrophe and lottery luck that would sink any franchise, in Indiana or on the Moon. And hand-waive we shall. But waive enough hands, and the cumulative effect of this bad luck will start slipping through our fingers unnoticed, like grains of sand piling up into a castle the size of the Gainbridge Fieldhouse, threatening to crush us all if we don’t make infrastructure improvements. I was out on the Pacers coming into the year, though I never found the time to publish that take anywhere preseason with the NFL kicking off and the MLB headed for the World Series and then World War III. — you’ll just have to trust my editors that I’ve been talking about it. My concern lay on the fact that a 50-32 Pacers team in 2024-25 had ridden one of the most absurd stretches of clutch shot-making ever to Game 7 of the NBA Finals, lost Tyrese Haliburton to a torn Achilles in one of the most heart-wrenching injuries in NBA history, lost said Game 7, lost Myles Turner to some Bucks stupidity and then went 19-63 (yes, that is nineteen and sixty-three ) the following year with a roster I thought … was not that bad. Every Pacers take I heard last year from people in NBA media more connected than I started and ended with the same two words: “gap year.” This 19-63 record was, of course, intentional, as the team tanked for a top draft pick to play when Haliburton was back the following season. But then they made a splashy move, wagering that draft pick on a bold 50-50 with the Clippers for Ivica Zubac, protecting that pick in a specific way that meant if it fell out of the top four, they would lose it. Well … it did, and their 19-63 record netted them nothing in one of the most stacked top fours we’ve ever seen. Once again: heartbreaking. Then the actual 2026 season rolled around, and their roster looked solid; at the very least, it would be competitive, if not actually a Finals contender in my mind. And it was going reasonably well for about seven minutes until Haliburton suffered a hamstring injury (like are you serious right now) and the rest of the team got injured along with him. Now 3-6, last week’s lineups would make you think they were tanking again. Their actual players will slowly make it back in time, but the question must officially be asked (no, not “is this team injury prone?” that’s a stupid question): do the Pacers have the roster to cope with even one injury, and can this group survive a wide-open but packed Eastern Conference, one with aspiring playoff teams popping out of drawers? item.title: Barry Sanders Sheds Light on Biggest What-If In Detroit Lions History
item.description: Imagine Barry Sanders and Joe Montana sharing the same backfield in Detroit. One of the greatest running backs in NFL history lining up behind one of the greatest quarterbacks to ever play the game. Two Hall of Famers, both capable of taking over a football game, wearing Honolulu blue and silver. For Detroit Lions fans who lived through the 1990s, it almost sounds too good to be true. But here’s the painful part: According to Barry Sanders, it nearly happened. During an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show , Sanders revisited the incredible story of how Montana wanted to join the Lions in 1993, only for Detroit’s front office to reject the opportunity. And judging by Sanders’ comments, he knows just how much that decision may have cost the franchise. item.title: Barcelona coaches closely monitoring teenage winger as he waits for first-team chance
item.description: Barcelona coaches closely monitoring teenage winger as he waits for first-team chance According to Mundo Deportivo , the Barcelona first-team coaching staff is keeping a close eye on the development of teenage summer signing Jesse Bisiwu. The 18-year-old winger is still waiting for his first competitive appearance for the senior setup, and as such, the coaches are monitoring his adaptation at the club. Bisiwu showing glimpses of potential Barcelona signed Bisiwu from Club Brugge in the summer in a deal worth €8.5 million plus add-ons. The teenage attacker was a personal bet by sporting director Deco and head of scouting Joao Amaral. The La Liga champions handed him a long-term contract until 2031 and included him in the first-team plans for pre-season, with the starlet even impressing in the friendly matches. Barcelona have great expectations of Bisiwu. (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website) However, that has not translated into an official first-team debut for Bisiwu as he has been largely playing with the club’s reserve team Barça Atletic. So far, the 18-year-old prodigy has made six league appearances for Juliano Belletti’s side, registering one assist in the process and showing fleeting glimpses of his immense talent and potential. While he has trained with the senior squad fairly regularly, Bisiwu has yet to be called up to the matchday squad even once by Hansi Flick. A disrupted start for Bisiwu However, Bisiwu’s introduction to life at Barcelona was not entirely straightforward. He suffered an injury during the Copa Catalunya final against CE Sabadell, leaving the pitch after just 10 minutes. Still awaiting his first-team debut. (Photo courtesy: FC Barcelona official website) There were other complications as well, as La Liga initially withheld his registration because of outstanding visa-related paperwork. Those interruptions have not helped his adaptation. As such, Barcelona’s coaching staff are continuing to closely monitor his progress rather than rushing him into the senior side. For now, Bisiwu’s aim is to continue developing with Barça Atletic and establish himself as a regular starter in Belletti’s team. As for opportunities with the first team, the youngster will have to bide his time. Flick, throughout his time at Barcelona, has shown that he will give young talent a chance if they impress. And that is what the young winger must aim to do.

From Liverpool’s perspective, interest in signing a new centre-back is more than understandable given question marks over the futures of Joe Gomez and Virgil van Dijk. item.title: Jordan Watkins has clear chance to continue coming out party
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 25: San Francisco wide receiver Jordan Watkins (17) attempts to catch a touchdown pass during the NFL game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Atlanta Falcons on October 25th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jordan Watkins was the major bright spot of the 49ers’ defeat to the Atlanta Falcons before their Week 8 bye, as the second-year wide receiver took advantage of the extra opportunities afforded to him by San Francisco’s injuries at the position. Watkins enjoyed a career day in the Niners’ 29-20 loss in Atlanta, catching three passes for 56 yards as he was targeted six times by Brock Purdy. One of Watkins’ targets looked to have gone for a touchdown when he appeared to have made a sensational diving leaping grab over a defender in the corner of the endzone in the fourth quarter, only to have that score wiped away following a replay review Watkins did not survive the ground having spectacularly managed to get both feet in bounds. Still, his performance in Atlanta is likely to have increased the faith Brock Purdy has in the former fourth-round pick. And Watkins is likely to have a chance to continue his coming out party as the 49ers return from their bye to face the Las Vegas Raiders, with top receiver Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel looking likely to miss another week. The 49ers look primed to get Demarcus Robinson back from injury, but there appears to be some doubt around Christian Kirk after he missed Thursday’s practice having only made his season debut against Atlanta. As such, the prospective absences of Evans, Samuel and perhaps Kirk give Watkins another chance to serve as one of Purdy’s top pass-catching weapons in Week 9. And the numbers suggest that opportunity is coming against an ideal opportunity. The Raiders have one of the worst pass defenses in the NFL, ranking 30th in the league by dropback success rate (47.4%) allowed and 25th in the league by dropback EPA per play. In other words, the Raiders allowing a little under half of the dropbacks against them to turn into successful plays, while they consistently struggle to prevent explosive passing plays. For a player with Watkins’ speed, the chance to go up against a defense so vulnerable to the big play represents an enticing matchup. Given the rapport he seemingly has with Purdy, he should view it as a game in which he could put together an even more impressive career day. With the continuation of the injury problems they are having at receiver, the 49ers would substantially benefit from having Watkins emerge as bonafide dynamic and reliable weapon in the offense. The Las Vegas defense is one that figures to be accommodating to the 49er passing game despite its injuries and, though San Francisco is in a desperate position in terms of options at wideout, for Watkins the conditions are perfect for a fully fledged breakout game.

item.title: The WTA Secretly Broadcast Its Players’ Private Conversations; How Is This Even Possible?
item.description: Aug 2, 2025; Montreal, QC, Canada; Rain delay on centre court and the WTA logo on the net during the match between Jessica Bouzas Maneiro (ESP) and Lin Zhu (CHN) in fourth round play at IGA Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Steen Kirby Imagine going to work, having a conversation with a colleague, perhaps saying something unflattering about another colleague, only to discover that your employer has been broadcasting the entire exchange to thousands of strangers on the internet. Now imagine that employer subsequently explaining that it had simply forgotten to tell you about the microphones. Welcome to the WTA Finals. On Wednesday, private conversations between players and coaches during practice sessions at Indian Wells were broadcast on the WTA’s official YouTube channel, with several recordings subsequently circulating across social media. The most prominent involved Jessica Pegula, who was overheard criticizing Mirra Andreeva’s behavior and describing the 19-year-old as a diva during a conversation with her coach, Mark Knowles. Another recording reportedly captured a tense exchange involving Elena Rybakina and her coach. Predictably, the internet had a wonderful time dissecting every word, but then came the truly extraordinary part. The WTA admitted that it had never informed the players that their conversations could be heard. Not that somebody hacked its equipment or that an unauthorized person secretly recorded a conversation. The WTA itself had installed microphones, broadcast the recordings, and apparently neglected the tiny detail of informing the people being recorded. Well, it would be truly difficult to devise a more spectacular failure of professional responsibility if the entire exercise had been organized by a committee specifically instructed to produce one. This Wasn’t a Leak Saying it so matters. The microphones were reportedly intended to capture the sounds of practice, allowing fans to enjoy a more immersive experience while watching their favourite players prepare for the season-ending championships. Okay, I guess. Tennis fans enjoy watching practice sessions, and there is certainly nothing wrong with giving them greater access to the sport, but somewhere between deciding to broadcast the sound of tennis balls and actually switching on the microphones, the WTA apparently forgot that human beings also possess the ability to speak. And that those human beings might occasionally discuss things they would rather not share with the entire planet. In its subsequent statement, the organization accepted full responsibility for failing to inform players and their teams that microphones were active. Great. The governing body of professional women’s tennis, an organization responsible for the interests of hundreds of athletes and the administration of a global sporting enterprise, has acknowledged that it failed to perform a task that would generally be considered fairly basic at a school

item.title: Fantasy Football Usage Report: Jonah Coleman primed for big Week 9 in expanded role
item.description: Last week featured several encouraging performances from young players we've spent all season waiting to step into key roles. This week, I highlight two rookies who could both have value as weekly streaming options going forward, or better, and a tight end who draws a plus matchup against one of the more porous defenses in the league. Without further delay, let's have a look at this week's usage report. RotoPat’s Week 9 Fantasy Football Rankings Ranking and evaluating all of Week 9’s top plays at quarterback, running back, receiver, tight end, kicker and defense. Patrick Daugherty , ▶ Running Backs Jonah Coleman (DEN) vs. Chiefs After missing four straight weeks with an ankle injury, Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman has found himself in a key role since returning in Week 7. That week, Coleman rushed nine times for 54 scoreless yards against the Cardinals while adding another two receptions for 15 yards. Last week, he followed it up with an 11-41-1 rushing line while adding another four receptions for 63 yards on five targets. Since Week 7, Coleman has been the fantasy RB12 in expected fantasy points (30.8 EP), and is leading the Broncos' backfield with a 26 percent opportunity share. His seven targets over that span also lead Denver's backfield, and with RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve, Coleman should have a valuable role as a pass-catcher for at least the next three weeks. His four rush attempts inside his opponent's five-yard line compared to J.K. Dobbins' one is also an encouraging sign heading into Week 9 against the Panthers. Coleman profiles as a fringe RB1/RB2 in a plus matchup against a Panthers run defense that has been among the worst in the league and is fresh off of firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. Saquon Barkley (PHI) vs. Commanders The Eagles have lost six straight games and are about to start their third different quarterback. Saquon Barkley , who is playing through a hamstring and back injury, has seen just 23 opportunities in his last two games since returning in Week 7 against the Cowboys. While he has still managed to finish as a top-24 PPR RB in back-to-back weeks, Barkley's production is fueled by good fortune in the touchdown department. He's found the end zone in each of his last two games, but those 12 combined PPR points make up 43.6 percent of his fantasy scoring over that span. Barkley was listed as a DNP on Wednesday but was limited in Thursday's practice and will presumably be good to go for Week 9's game against the Giants. That said, the lack of volume (11.5 opps/gm) over the last two weeks, coupled with Philly's offensive struggles, makes him hard to trust against a Giants defense that has allowed the sixth-fewest PPR points per game (18.0) to opposing RBs in its last five games. Until his volume sees a bit of an uptick, Barkley is starting to profile more like a fringe RB2/RB3. item.description: Seattle Sounders face historic stakes in Decision Day clash with LAFC By Ari Liljenwall For nearly two decades, Seattle Sounders FC have been synonymous with the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs. The Sounders have failed to qualify for the postseason just once since joining MLS in 2009. They've also reached MLS Cup presented by Audi four times, winning league titles in 2016 and 2019. But now, when hosting Saturday’s Decision Day showdown with LAFC , the Sounders face the possibility of a second postseason miss in 18 MLS seasons, the other coming in 2022 (7 pm ET | Apple TV ). Seattle enter Decision Day below the playoff line at 10th in the Western Conference standings, tied with the Portland Timbers and Colorado Rapids on 43 points but trailing both on tiebreakers. They'll likely need to defeat LAFC to get in, plus get some help elsewhere. A draw and other favorable results could also tilt the scales in their favor. “Personally, I don’t like it,” head coach Brian Schmetzer said this week. “I mean, we shot ourselves in the foot in multiple, multiple games. “I don’t like the position we’re in. But that’s reality, and we’re facing reality and trying to make sure that we do everything we can to get a result on Saturday.” Picking up the pieces Seattle's predicament worsened after last weekend's 5-1 defeat at Cascadia rivals Vancouver Whitecaps FC , marking the club's fifth straight winless match after finding steam in recent months. The Vancouver setback prompted Schmetzer to take an unconventional approach to preparing his team for their regular-season finale. Rather than review film of the Vancouver defeat with the full squad, Schmetzer invited players to identify areas they believe need improvement, opening the floor for candid conversations. I’m not going to give the details away of everything that went on in there. item.description: Previewing the Green Bay Packers (5-3) versus the New England Patriots (5-3) in Week 9 action: How to watch The Packers and Patriots will play in "America's Game of the Week" on FOX in the late afternoon timeslot on Sunday. Most of the country will get Packers-Patriots, which is in red below: Packers-Patriots head-to-head The Packers lead the all-time series with the Patriots 7-6, including a win in Super Bowl XXXI following the 1996 season and an overtime win at Lambeau Field during the last meeting in 2022. The Packers haven't won in New England since the 2002 season, when Brett Favre threw three touchdown passes in a 28-10 win over the defending Super Bowl champs. The last meeting at Gillette Stadium ended in a 31-17 win for Brady, Bill Belichick and the Patriots on "Sunday Night Football" in 2018. Arguably the best game in the Aaron Rodgers vs. Tom Brady era came in 2014 at Lambeau Field, when the Packers escaped with a 26-21 win over the eventual champions. Last week Both the Packers and Patriots improved to 5-3 overall with wins in Week 8. Mike Vrabel's team trailed 13-3 at the half in Miami last Sunday but scored 21 straight points in the second half and snuck past Jeff Hafley and the Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. item.description: It is about eight months since England’s men last trod the Twickenham turf, a long gap between hit-outs on home soil. That performance against Ireland will carry few happy memories for Steve Borthwick ’s squad – not that there is any conscious effort to right the wrongs. “If we’re going to sit and stew over a game eight months ago, we’re in f***** trouble,” a surprisingly spiky Richard Wigglesworth, the senior assistant coach, remarked this week. Still, England would be wise to reflect on their failings in that game. While there was plenty to learn from a lean Six Nations, it was that showing in the 42-21 defeat that most disappointed Borthwick and his selection, falling so far short of where they needed to be . It was at the breakdown where Ireland beasted them particularly, and in the two red zones especially: Andy Farrell’s side won 14 turnovers and limited England to just 1.3 points per 22 entry. England were heavily beaten by Ireland in the Six Nations (PA Wire) England’s difficulty at the breakdown was striking given their selection. That game remains Henry Pollock ’s only start at Test level; a back row of he, Tom Curry and Ben Earl should have provided plenty of ruck menace. But, perhaps, Borthwick was guilty of a redundancy of skillset. While Pollock and Earl are enterprising and prolific carriers, neither is a consistent resourcer of rucks; Curry, too, per Opta hit just 11.7 rucks per 80 minutes for Sale across the last Prem campaign, less than half that of Guy Pepper, a significant absentee for this campaign. That may be partly to do with Bath’s multi-phase preference, and also Curry’s usage as an edge forward in attack. That combined with the typically unpredictable weather in southeastern Brazil have produced some of the most memorable grands prix in the history of the sport. Kimi Antonelli already clinched the world drivers' championship last weekend in Mexico City, becoming the youngest ever to do so. But behind him, quite an intense race is developing as just 16 points separate Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second place (261) and Ferrari's Charles Leclerc in fifth (245) with four rounds remaining. On the constructors' side, Mercedes can clinch that title by merely out-scoring Ferrari by three points in Brazil this weekend. The Scuderia do have a healthy 122-point edge over Red Bull in third place, but defending champion McLaren are just 17 points behind in fourth. Ferrari drama persists Despite being in the second in the constructors's standings, all is not harmonious in the Ferrari camp . The latest incident between teammates Hamilton and Leclerc came during the first lap in Mexico City as going into Turn, they held the top two spots. But two aggressive moves from Leclerc, first into Turn 1, then into Turn 4, set off a chain of events that handed Verstappen the lead and eventual race win. Hamilton lamented on the radio in the closing moments of the race that "serious" talks need to be had. Mexico City was just the latest in a series of incidents between the teammates that began at Zandvoort and continued at Monza, costing the team valuable results . "Well, I'll speak with Lewis," Leclerc said . "I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off the track out of Turn 1, but I think it's racing. When you are fighting for a win, it's the way it should be." Hamilton continued to fume this week: "When I was at Mercedes, I watched and witnessed the back and forth between Charles and Carlos [Sainz] several races, where they were battling so much that the person ahead just pulled away, and they had the pace to actually win. "But it is one thing when that's happening in fourth and fifth, as opposed to first and second, and you lose the win. That's significant. "The guy is 28 years old, so I don't think it's an age thing. I think it's a mentality thing. "It's like, ‘Do or die. Either I win or none of us do,’ and it shouldn't be that. It should be us getting that one-two." item.description: Why Troilo’s Argentina call-up is being labelled ‘revenge’ on Inter midfielder Barella Parma defender Mariano Troilo has recently earned his first call-up to the Argentina national team squad from Lionel Scaloni, which media outlets in Italy are calling ‘revenge’ on Inter midfielder Nicolo Barella following a spat between the pair at the end of last season. Here’s what happened. Troilo is one of seven Serie A players involved in the latest Argentina national team squad , along with Roma trio Leonardo Balerdi, Matias Soule and Santiago Castro, Como pair Nico Paz and Maxi Perrone, as well as Fiorentina’s Franco Mastantuono. On Thursday, LIV Golf confirmed in court that it would shut down and liquidate its remaining assets after B.C. Partners withdrew from a proposed $300 million investment that had been intended to keep the league afloat and facilitate its restructuring. The timing wasn't lost on some players. item.title: Xabi Alonso reacts to Cole Palmer's surprise omission from England squad
item.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has reaffirmed his faith in Cole Palmer after the attacker was a surprise omission from the latest England squad. Thomas Tuchel reiterated his concern that Palmer “misses too many opportunities to impress” when he announced his squad for the November international break on Friday morning. Palmer withdrew from the squad for the October window and Tuchel criticised him at the time for missing “too many camps with injuries”, and the German has opted to keep faith with the majority of the squad he picked then, rather than reinstate the 24-year-old. Palmer has not played for England since March and missed out on the World Cup squad after struggling with injuries last season. Speaking to media before Chelsea’s trip to Sunderland this Sunday, Alonso said he had not spoken to Palmer about the England squad for this Nations League campaign but added that he was “very happy” with his player. Chelsea informed the England set-up that Palmer was fit and available for selection, and he has made a strong start to the season, starting each of the Blues’ nine Premier League games and registering five goals and three assists in 11 games across all competitions. He has also formed a successful attacking partnership with Morgan Rogers , who has made the Three Lions squad. Tuchel said he had enough No 10s for this round of fixtures, with Morgan Gibbs-White , Eberechi Eze , and Jude Bellingham selected as well as Rogers, while versatile players Josh King and Jobe Bellingham have been called up for the first time. Alonso said: “We are very happy with Cole. I think he is enjoying his game, he is connecting very well with the other attackers. He is helping the team with developing and improving what we want to achieve, knowing that everything takes time but I am very happy with his quality, his attitude and the impact he is having on the rest of the team.” Asked whether he had discussed Palmer’s ambitions to get back into the England squad with him or any regrets over his decision to pull out from the last camp, Alonso said: “We haven't spoken about that. We are focussed on our things, on Chelsea things and how to do better and how to help him and how he can become more and more influential on the game. Those are our topics to talk. “We speak about Chelsea. We have enough on our plate. My impact area is my control area and what we talk about.” Alonso also dismissed concerns that the decision to omit Palmer would be a test of his character, saying: “He needs to focus on his thing - and his thing is to play good football and enjoy his game with us, with Chelsea.”

item.title: Carrick insists Man Utd can recapture former glories
item.description: Manchester United's match against Aston Villa could decide Michael Carrick's future (Oli SCARFF) Michael Carrick said patience is needed to restore Manchester United to their former glory as he prepares for Sunday's clash against Aston Villa, which could be his final match in charge. United snapped a nine-game winless run with a thrilling fightback from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League on Tuesday. The Red Devils have not won in the Premier League since August and sit outside the relegation zone only on goal difference. Carrick has been handed a stay of execution by the United board but a two-week international break following the Villa match gives them an opportunity to make a change unless he can prove his team are on the right track. The former midfielder was part of United's golden age under former manager Alex Ferguson, during which they won multiple major trophies. The club's fortunes have declined significantly since the Scot retired after the club's last Premier League title-winning season in 2013. Carrick, though, dismissed the suggestion it is impossible for United to recreate the success that Ferguson built. "It's not impossible. Anything is possible," he told a pre-match press conference on Friday. "The recent history that we've had and where we want to get to, it's not going to happen in the blink of an eye -- it's not going to happen overnight. "Success does take time and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build. "We showed a really quick response and improved a lot last season and you know it shows what is possible, but again sustaining it is the key, consistency is the key. "There's no other way of doing it. There's no shortcuts to it and in the end that's where you get to, but it's definitely possible." Victory over Roma was marred by the loss of £70 million ($93 million) signing Carlos Baleba for the foreseeable future with a hamstring injury.
